hero.headline: Stuart downtown dock to close Monday for $3 million renovation, doubling boat capacity
hero.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will shut down July 6 to undergo a $3 million renovation expected to take one year, with work finishing by next Fourth of July. The project represents a significant expansion of the facility, nearly doubling its capacity from 18 to 44 slips that will accommodate both motorized and non-motorized vessels. More than 1,400 boaters rely on the dock annually, making the upgrade an important investment for the community's waterfront infrastructure.

The renovation will feature a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed emphasized that the improvements serve a dual purpose beyond simply adding capacity. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. The project receives funding through a state grant and transportation impact fees, spreading the financial burden across multiple sources.

The city has worked proactively to ensure that businesses depending on the dock can continue operating during the closure. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which runs passenger boarding operations from the facility, initially worried about its ability to function during construction. However, Austin Kuyrkendall, the company's director of operations, confirmed that officials found a workable solution. "So they're allowing us to build a gate right here at the end of the downtown Stuart dock. This is the non-floating section, but still we're going to be able to open this up and board people right here," Kuyrkendall said.

Kuyrkendall highlighted the dock's importance to Stuart's character and economic vitality. "Stuart is not Stuart without the water," he noted. He acknowledged the challenges the current facility faces, particularly when demand is high. "On the weekend that's when it can get a little hectic at the dock and you know it's never great for us when we're squeezing in and trying to find spots," Kuyrkendall said. Boat captain Parker Fisher, based in Stuart, supports the improvements. "It's definitely needed some work over the years, so I'm glad they're putting money into it," Fisher said. The modernization and expansion of the dock should benefit not only businesses but the broader community by creating more opportunities for boaters and strengthening Stuart's waterfront infrastructure for years to come.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County zoning board recommends denial of data center near Arden, Saddle View Elementary
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School in western Palm Beach County. The recommendation followed a nearly five-hour public hearing at the Vista Center that drew more than 100 attendees, with more than 40 residents speaking during public comment. The proposed facility would be built approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and the recently opened Saddle View Elementary School. The project now heads to the Palm Beach County Commission, which will make the final decision during a July 15 public hearing.

One of the central issues during Thursday's hearing was how the project should be classified under the county's land development code. Board members questioned whether the proposed data center qualifies as light industrial or should instead be considered heavy industrial. Under county regulations, light industrial uses cannot create impacts beyond their property lines. Board members said they were not presented with enough evidence to conclude the facility would meet that standard. Residents raised concerns about potential health, safety, environmental and noise impacts. Resident Laura Cole voiced concerns about low-frequency hum that penetrates glass and concrete. Project developer Ernie Cox said he was disappointed by the board's recommendation but plans to use the feedback from Thursday's hearing to strengthen his case before county commissioners.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances plan to donate land for new Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council has approved the first reading of an ordinance to transfer 7 acres of city-owned land to the Florida Department of Transportation to support construction of a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike at Midway Road. The council is scheduled to vote on final approval at a future meeting. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, the new interchange will close a substantial gap in Turnpike access points currently available to city residents and commuters. The project is designed to support both the growth that has already taken place in Port St. Lucie and anticipated expansion over the next 20 to 50 years.

The partial interchange is part of a larger effort to improve transportation infrastructure in the area. FDOT is managing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project, which aims to reduce congestion and improve safety. The first phase of construction is currently underway, widening Midway Road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, which will extend from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in summer 2027. Beyond road widening, the project will incorporate bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks.

The partial interchange remains in the design phase as FDOT works on multiple elements of the transportation improvement. The department is simultaneously working on improving the Turnpike bridge itself. Samples emphasized that the interchange represents a focus on accessibility and accommodating the city's ongoing growth. "This is a way for us to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years," Samples said.

The construction activity has been visible to Port St. Lucie residents. One area resident, Erin Scheumeister, acknowledged that while the ongoing work can be disruptive, she recognizes its necessity. "We definitely needed it to be expanded," Scheumeister said. "It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." As construction continues on the Midway Road project and planning advances for the Turnpike interchange, city officials expect the improvements will enhance transportation efficiency for the expanding community.

cards.headline: Glydways proposes elevated self-driving transit connecting West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: California-based autonomous transit company Glydways is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The system would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport using small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. The company estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. The proposal would also connect the Brightline station and nearby transportation hubs that currently lack easy pedestrian or traveler connections.

While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price tag, Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity. He referenced previous South Florida light rail discussions that estimated $400 million to $500 million per mile and argued Glydways would come in far below that range. Potential funding sources include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal. Glydways currently operates a testing facility in California and has a project under construction near Atlanta's airport expected to begin offering rides by year's end.

Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, and nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would function like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without traffic delays or multiple intermediate stops. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

Tuesday's County Commission meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal. If commissioners move forward, the county could seek competing bids and begin discussions on routes, station locations, costs and financing, with a planning and design contract potentially awarded later this year.

cards.headline: Delray Beach golf training center Tee Box opens July 17 after $90,000 contractor delay
cards.teaser: Tee Box, a virtual golf training and performance center on Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard near Delray Beach, will open July 17 after a three-month delay and $90,000 in repairs caused by contractor problems.
cards.body:
Tee Box, a virtual golf training and performance center on Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard near Delray Beach, will open July 17 after a three-month delay caused by contractor problems. Owner Tom Molen said the project was scheduled to open in April but was postponed after the licensed contractor hired to prepare the space failed to complete the work properly. The work had to be redone, resulting in what Molen estimated as a $90,000 job. That figure does not include lost revenue during the delays or the cost of hiring another contractor to fix the problems. "It was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall," Molen said.

David Allan, founder of Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, said contractor-related issues are impacting a significant number of people across Palm Beach County. He estimates 25 to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners face major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have proper licenses and insurance before any work begins. According to Allan, the most common contractor complaints in Palm Beach County involve roofing, windows and air conditioning work.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets roof fixed and lien removed after WPTV investigation
cards.teaser: Lantana homeowner Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran, had a nearly $7,000 lien removed from his home and unfinished roof repairs completed after WPTV contacted the contractor.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season. He made six payments totaling more than $17,000 to the company but said they left two holes unfinished on the back of his home and stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails starting in January. Screenshots McCoy shared with WPTV show he contacted the company between January 10 and February 5, when a worker said the owner would call him. The owner never did, according to McCoy.

The situation worsened when Gulfeagle Supply filed a nearly $7,000 lien on McCoy's home, claiming Seabreeze Roofing had not paid for materials furnished for the property. McCoy worried he would need to hire an attorney or go to court. After WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized was delivered to McCoy within an hour. The contractor also sent crews back to complete the roof repairs, with McCoy sending WPTV a photo of the work being finished about an hour after he received the waiver.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit rescued two boaters Wednesday after their small motorized boat took on water and became submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway. Both occupants were wearing life jackets.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1, thanks to a quick response from St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets. The marine unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life and expressed gratitude that the call ended safely and pride in the swift response by Marine Unit deputies.

Treasure Coast school districts continued to show growth in the state's latest assessment results. All three Treasure Coast school districts earned top grades from the Florida Department of Education. hero.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof fixed after WPTV investigates contractor
hero.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, had a nearly $7,000 lien placed on his home after his roofing contractor allegedly failed to pay for materials.
hero.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his aging roof before hurricane season. McCoy made six payments totaling more than $17,000 to complete the project. While he was generally satisfied with most of the work, the company left two holes unfinished on the back side of his home. When McCoy tried to contact the contractor about these repairs through calls, texts, and emails between January and February, the company stopped responding to his attempts.

The situation worsened when McCoy received letters from Gulfeagle Supply warning that a nearly $7,000 lien had been filed against his home with the county. According to the lien document, Gulfeagle Supply had provided materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but had not been paid for those supplies. McCoy said he felt sick about the situation and worried that he would need to hire an attorney and go to court to resolve the matter, which he knew would cost thousands of dollars.

After WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey contacted the owner of Seabreeze Roofing directly to ask about the unpaid materials and the lien, the situation changed dramatically. Within an hour, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien that had been signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized. McCoy was shocked by the rapid resolution. "Oh my God, how did you do that? Are you serious?" he asked. He also learned that the contractor would return to fix the two unfinished areas on his roof.

About an hour after receiving the lien waiver, McCoy sent WPTV a photo showing crews back on his roof completing the work. McCoy expressed his overwhelming relief after months of frustration and worry. "I've been going through hell," he said. "I have not gotten a response, not even a phone call from these people in months." He added that the lien removal felt like a tremendous burden had been lifted from his shoulders. "I felt like crying," McCoy said. "You just don't know how much of a burden this was off of me."

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. The interchange will help accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, both currently in the design phase. The project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Marine Unit rescues two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters ended up in the water Wednesday after their small motorized boat took on water and became submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway, but life jackets kept them afloat until deputies arrived.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Sunday for year-long $3 million renovation
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades serve multiple purposes beyond capacity expansion. The improvements will prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses and boaters who rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock on the non-floating section to board passengers. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the dock plays a central role in the city's identity and economy, noting that weekends can get hectic with boats squeezing in to find spots.

cards.headline: Mobile and manufactured homeowners can access $167 million in Florida repair funding starting in August
cards.teaser: Senate Bill 594 took effect Wednesday, opening up $167 million in state affordable housing funding to help mobile and manufactured home owners pay for emergency repairs and storm-hardening retrofits.
cards.body:
Senate Bill 594 took effect July 1, opening up $167 million in state affordable housing funding to help mobile and manufactured home owners pay for emergency repairs and storm-hardening retrofits. Julie Stellatos with Martin County Human Services says an online portal will open in August. Once it does, about 75 percent of the county's annual SHIP funding, typically $1 million to $1.5 million, could now help eligible mobile and manufactured homeowners. People can either fill out an online application or call the office to have one mailed to them.

The change follows an investigation that exposed hundreds of thousands of older homes across Florida that cannot stand up to today's storms. It started with an EF-3 tornado that obliterated manufactured homes in the Spanish Lakes Country Club Community of Fort Pierce. Spanish Lakes resident Paula Richards said the community lost 138 homes and six friends were killed. The investigation found nearly 700,000, about two-thirds of Florida's more than 1 million mobile and manufactured homes, were built before today's federal safety standards, leaving them unable to withstand modern storms. Okeechobee County officials said they are updating the county's local housing assistance plan to comply with the new law and plans to offer lot rent, rehabilitation and emergency repair assistance for manufactured home owners once the program opens.

cards.headline: Delray Beach golf training center Tee Box delayed three months and $90,000 by contractor problems
cards.teaser: Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center preparing to open near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, says contractor issues delayed the opening from April to July.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center preparing to open near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, said the project was delayed by three months after problems with the contractor hired to prepare the space. Instead of opening on schedule in April, Molen said the work was constantly pushed off. Even though the contractor was licensed, Molen said the work ultimately had to be redone, creating a costly domino effect. Molen estimated the issues cost him $90,000, not including revenue lost during the delays or the added expense of bringing in another contractor to fix the problems. He said it was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall.

David Allan, founder of Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, said contractor-related issues are impacting a significant number of people across Palm Beach County. He estimates 25 to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners face major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have the proper licenses and insurance before any work begins. According to Allan, the most common contractor complaints in Palm Beach County involve roofing, windows and air conditioning work. After months of delays and repairs, Tee Box is preparing for its grand opening set for July 17.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach woman raises funds for best friend's family after Venezuela earthquakes kill relatives
cards.teaser: Carla Alvarado of West Palm Beach launched a GoFundMe campaign to support her best friend Alessandra De La Correa's family after two devastating earthquakes struck Venezuela's coastal city of La Guaira.
cards.body:
Alessandra De La Correa spent six agonizing hours wondering whether her parents were alive after two devastating earthquakes struck Venezuela's coastal city of La Guaira last week, collapsing buildings and killing members of her family. Her best friend since high school, Carla Alvarado, who now lives in West Palm Beach, woke De La Correa with nonstop phone calls in the middle of the night after the earthquakes struck. De La Correa's parents survived, but several relatives did not. The family lost her 17-year-old cousin Claudia, who had planned to study dentistry and was rehearsing a dance routine with classmates when the building collapsed. They also lost her grandmother, uncle and uncle's wife.

The losses came just weeks after De La Correa returned from her first visit to Venezuela in several years, where she had traveled to announce she and her partner are expecting a baby. The earthquakes also destroyed her parents' home and businesses, including her mother's children's clothing store located in a shopping mall that collapsed entirely. Feeling powerless from abroad, Alvarado launched a GoFundMe campaign aiming to raise $15,000 to support De La Correa's relatives. De La Correa said the support from friends and strangers has become a lifeline as her parents return daily to the ruins of their apartment building searching for salvageable belongings.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting season programs through September
hero.teaser: The center is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season, including guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program and Hatchling Releases.
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering a variety of educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season this summer. The center said guests can participate in seasonal experiences through September, including guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to Loggerhead Marinelife Center, the programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The center's Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations during the programs may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. Loggerhead Marinelife Center also said its education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success.

Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach hosts Fourth of July celebration with fireworks and America 250 events
cards.body:
North Palm Beach will celebrate Independence Day on July 4 with a full day of free, family-friendly activities at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse. The event recognizes America's 250th anniversary alongside traditional Independence Day festivities.

The celebration begins at 11 a.m. with a community pool party at the country club pool area, featuring a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages, and a poolside satellite bar. At 4:30 p.m., families can participate in lawn games including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga and face painting. The Clubhouse will serve a Fourth of July barbecue buffet starting at 4:30 p.m. Live music from Solstice Reign is scheduled to begin around 6 p.m. Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, noted that the golf course offers one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display, which concludes the event at 9 p.m. For registration information and additional details, attendees should contact North Palm Beach Country Club.

hero.headline: Democratic first responder Bernard Taylor raises $563,000 in second quarter for Congressional District 21 race
hero.teaser: Bernard Taylor, an EMT/paramedic challenging Republican U.S. Rep. Brian Mast, announced his campaign raised just under $563,000 in the second quarter with more than 25,000 individual donations averaging $22 each.
hero.body:
Democratic congressional candidate Bernard Taylor, an EMT/paramedic, reported raising just under $563,000 during the second quarter of 2025 for his campaign to challenge Republican U.S. Rep. Brian Mast in Florida's 21st Congressional District. The fundraising haul came from more than 25,000 individual donations that averaged $22 each between April 1 and June 30. Taylor's campaign emphasized that it declined all corporate PAC money and special-interest donations, with more than 93 percent of contributions coming through mobile devices and approximately 41 percent processed through the digital fundraising platform ActBlue.

Taylor, a fourth-generation Floridian, said the fundraising results demonstrate support from working families, retirees, veterans, teachers, and first responders rather than wealthy interests. "I'm humbled by the incredible support we've received from thousands of people who believe it's time for new leadership in Washington," Taylor stated. "These contributions are coming from working families, retirees, veterans, teachers, first responders, and neighbors who want a representative who understands their challenges and will fight for them every day." His campaign platform prioritizes affordable healthcare access, educational investment, job creation, housing affordability, environmental protection, and representing constituents over political insiders. Taylor said his background in emergency medical services has shown him the real-world consequences of rising healthcare costs and limited options facing families across the district.

The coastal district stretches from Royal Palm Lake in Palm Beach County north through Martin and St. Lucie counties. About 57.5 percent of voters in the district voted for President Donald Trump in 2024 under new congressional map boundaries that Gov. Ron DeSantis and the Republican-dominated Legislature approved in April. Taylor faces a primary opponent in U.S. Coast Guard veteran James Martin, who entered the second quarter with nearly $307,000 raised. Taylor had raised only $32,500 before this quarter after filing for the race in April 2025, according to Federal Election Commission records. "We are grateful for what we accomplished in Q2, and we are looking forward to an even stronger Q3," Taylor said.

Republican incumbent Mast entered April with more than $2.5 million in cash on hand. Other candidates running in the race include independent Alexander Cooke and write-in candidate David Fabrikant.

cards.headline: Florida records lowest residential arson rate in nation during July, FBI data shows
cards.teaser: Florida has the lowest rate of residential arson in the country during July, according to a new analysis of FBI crime data.
cards.body:
Florida has the nation's lowest rate of residential arson during July, according to a new analysis of FBI crime data. The state averages just 17.8 residential arson incidents each year over the last five Julys, roughly one incident for every 586,000 homes. A study conducted by Besroi Roofing and Siding using FBI Crime Data Explorer records from 2021 through 2025 ranked all 50 states by July residential arson rates. Florida edged out New Jersey for the top spot and dramatically outperformed neighboring states, where residential arson rates were significantly higher. Georgia's residential arson rate was roughly four times higher than Florida's, while Alabama's was roughly 10 times higher. Florida's July residential arson rate is approximately one-sixth the national average, despite the state having the country's third-largest housing market.

The timing of the report comes as millions of Floridians prepare to celebrate Independence Day with backyard barbecues and fireworks. Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson and the Florida Forest Service spent the lead-up to the Fourth of July reminding residents that even though drought conditions are easing, wildfire season remains active and fireworks should be used responsibly. While intentional residential fires are rare in Florida, the Forest Service and firefighters across the state emphasize that accidental fires remain a concern during holiday weekends when firework use peaks.

cards.headline: Former Governor Charlie Crist gains endorsement from state Rep. Allison Tant in St. Petersburg mayoral race
cards.teaser: State Rep. Allison Tant endorsed former Governor Charlie Crist's campaign for St. Petersburg Mayor, citing their decadeslong political relationship and his record of public service through roles as state Senator, Governor and Congressman.
cards.body:
Former Florida Governor Charlie Crist received an endorsement from state Rep. Allison Tant for his campaign for St. Petersburg Mayor. Tant announced her support Thursday, citing her decades-long political relationship with Crist through his service as state Senator, Governor and Congressman. "He shows up, he listens, he rolls up his sleeves and takes action to address the work of caring for others and his community," Tant said, adding that "He will be an excellent Mayor." Crist praised Tant for her career advocating for students, families and Floridians with disabilities, as well as her service as a former Chair of the Florida Democratic Party. "That is the kind of leadership I'll bring to my hometown," Crist said.

The endorsement announcement comes days after Crist unveiled a larger slate of Democratic leaders supporting his campaign against incumbent Mayor Ken Welch. The group includes U.S. Rep. Lois Frankel, former U.S. Reps. Cheri Bustos of Illinois and Matt Cartwright of Pennsylvania, state Sen. Darryl Rouson, former state Rep. Ben Diamond, former Department of Juvenile Justice Secretary and state Rep. Frank Peterman, and current and former Tampa and St. Petersburg City Council members. The nonpartisan St. Petersburg mayoral race has drawn significant attention from Democratic officials and activists. City Council Member Brandi Gabbard is also polling with double digit support in the race.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Police union endorses Belinda Keiser for Congressional District 22 seat
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach Police Benevolent Association endorsed Republican congressional candidate Belinda Keiser for Florida's 22nd Congressional District, calling her a strong law and order conservative.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Police Benevolent Association announced its endorsement of Republican Belinda Keiser in her campaign for Florida's 22nd Congressional District. John Kazanjian, President of the Palm Beach Police Benevolent Association, said Keiser is a strong law and order conservative who understands the importance of protecting and supporting law enforcement. Kazanjian stated that in Washington, Keiser will effectively advocate for the needs of law enforcement, defend the rule of law, hold criminals accountable and keep communities safe. The union asked its members, their friends and families, and all citizens of Palm Beach County who respect law enforcement to vote for Keiser.

Keiser, Vice Chancellor of Keiser University, said she is deeply honored to receive the endorsement and promised to fight to ensure law enforcement has the resources, training and support needed to do their jobs safely and effectively. She noted that Keiser University made a Multiple Interactive Learning Objective simulator available for criminal justice and homeland security students. Keiser is one of seven Republicans who qualified to run for the open seat. A new congressional map enacted this year by Gov. Ron DeSantis left the seat with no natural incumbent. Under the new lines, about 55% of voters in Congressional District 22 supported Republican Donald Trump in the 2024 Presidential Election.

cards.headline: Tampa aerospace firm TRAK TECOM produces components for F-35 fighter aircraft, supports 700 regional jobs
cards.teaser: Tampa-based TRAK TECOM designs RF assemblies and defense antenna systems for the F-35 Lightning II, contributing to an aerospace supply chain that supports more than 700 jobs and generates $150 million in annual economic impact in the Tampa Bay region.
cards.body:
TRAK TECOM, a Tampa-based aerospace and defense company, has specialized in designing RF assemblies and SATCOM antenna systems for more than 65 years. The company develops advanced RF microwave assemblies, circulators, multichannel switch filter banks, low-silhouette blade antennas and other critical technologies for the F-35 Lightning II fighter aircraft. These components are central to the aircraft's ability to communicate, share data and maintain situational awareness in contested environments.

The F-35 program connects a supply chain of nearly 1,900 businesses nationwide, with more than 160 based in Florida. In the Tampa Bay region, the F-35 and its supply chain generate a $150 million annual economic impact and more than 700 direct jobs, including dozens of small businesses and veteran-owned suppliers. Statewide, the program supports more than 30,000 jobs and generates an estimated $23 billion in economic impact. Nineteen nations have partnered with the United States to purchase and field the F-35, strengthening interoperability and collective defense. Jennifer Cruise, a MarCom Manager for TRAK TECOM, noted that employees take immense pride in knowing their work directly supports the warfighter.

cards.headline: Democratic PAC Engage Y'All endorses 22 Florida candidates in congressional and legislative races
cards.teaser: Engage Y'All endorsed two congressional candidates and 16 legislative candidates across Florida, focusing on seats the PAC believes Democrats can flip in November.
cards.body:
Democratic PAC Engage Y'All announced endorsements of 22 Florida candidates ahead of the November election, including two congressional candidates and 16 running for legislative seats, plus several local candidates. The PAC endorsed Pia Dandiya in the open Florida's 22nd Congressional District race and Nicole Locklin in a challenge to Republican U.S. Rep. Mario Díaz-Balart in Florida's 26th Congressional District. In state Senate races, the PAC endorsed Lauren Donahoo in Senate District 2, held by Republican state Sen. Corey Simon, and Ashley Gantt in Senate District 34, which opened as Democratic state Sen. Shevrin Jones runs for Congress.

The House race endorsements include Jane Aman in House District 37, Lucai Baez-Geller in House District 106, Darryl Block in House District 36, Daniel Cicirelli in House District 31, Kyandra Darling in House District 62, Michelle DeJesus in House District 38, Jared Fox in House District 39, Eric Gray in House District 35, August Mangeney in House District 93, Justin Mendoza-Routt in House District 113, May Thach in House District 61, John Taylor in House District 109, Samuel Vilchez Santiago in House District 43 and Ingrid Wadsworth in House District 2. All but three are currently GOP-held seats. Local endorsements include Palm Coast City Council candidate Dee Galery, St. Petersburg City Council candidate Linsey Grove, Orange County School Board candidate Susanne Peña, and Polk County School Board Member Victor Sims. The endorsements included 59% women, 50% people of color, and 86% members of the millennial and Generation Z demographics.

cards.headline: Florida puts hundreds of millions toward housing affordability in new state budget
cards.teaser: The Florida state budget allocates hundreds of millions of dollars toward housing affordability initiatives.
cards.body:
Florida's new state budget includes hundreds of millions of dollars directed toward housing affordability programs. The funding represents a major allocation in the state's fiscal plan to address housing costs affecting residents across Florida. Details about specific programs and distribution methods were outlined in the budget legislation.

The housing affordability funding comes as Florida continues to experience growth in population and housing demand. State officials have identified affordable housing as a priority area requiring significant financial resources. The budget allocation will support various initiatives aimed at making housing more accessible to Florida residents.

hero.headline: Woman dies after being pulled from burning home in Hobe Sound
hero.teaser: A woman died after being pulled from a burning home in Hobe Sound on Thursday.
hero.body: A woman died after being pulled from a burning home in Hobe Sound on Thursday. The incident occurred in the Hobe Sound community in Martin County. The victim's identity has not been released.

cards.headline: Four Martin County teens arrested after 14-year-old robbed at gunpoint
cards.teaser: Four teenagers in Martin County were arrested after a 14-year-old boy was robbed at gunpoint, leading deputies on a chase.
cards.body:
Four teenagers in Martin County were arrested after a 14-year-old boy was robbed at gunpoint on Thursday. The suspects led Martin County deputies on a chase following the alleged robbery.

The arrests came after the incident involving the teenage victim. Details about where the robbery occurred and the identities of the arrested teens were not immediately released.

cards.headline: St. Lucie marine deputies rescue two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters were rescued Wednesday after their small motorized boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit deputies and their decision to wear life jackets. The Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. The sheriff's office said in a Facebook post that the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life, and expressed gratitude that the call ended safely while praising the swift response by Marine Unit deputies.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Council approves land transfer for Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved giving 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to the Turnpike.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to transfer 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at the Florida Turnpike. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, there is a significant gap between current Turnpike entrances and exits in the city. Samples said the interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety concerns. The first phase involves widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road, which is currently under construction. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to transfer the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Zoning Commission recommends denial of controversial data center near Arden
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend denial of Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School in western Palm Beach County. The recommendation followed a nearly five-hour public hearing at the Vista Center that drew more than 100 attendees, with more than 40 residents speaking during public comment. The proposed facility would be built approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and the recently opened Saddle View Elementary School.

Board members questioned whether the proposed data center qualifies as light industrial or should instead be considered heavy industrial. Under county regulations, light industrial uses cannot create impacts beyond their property lines. Board members said they were not presented with enough evidence to conclude the facility would meet that standard. The board's recommendation comes after Palm Beach County planning staff recommended approval of the project. The project now heads to the Palm Beach County Commission, which will make the final decision during a July 15 public hearing. Residents raised concerns about potential health, safety, environmental and noise impacts. Project developer Ernie Cox said he was disappointed by the recommendation but plans to provide additional information before the July 15 meeting.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran's roof completed and lien removed after contractor dispute
cards.teaser: A Lantana homeowner had a nearly $7,000 lien removed from his home and unfinished roof repairs completed after months of frustration with a roofing contractor.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, turned to WPTV for help after months of frustration with Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach. McCoy paid the company more than $17,000 in six payments to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season but said the contractor left two holes unfinished on the back of his home and stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails starting in January. A worker responded to one email on Feb. 5 saying the owner would call, but McCoy said that call never came.

The situation worsened when Gulfeagle Supply, which furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing, filed a nearly $7,000 lien against McCoy's home. McCoy worried he would need to hire an attorney or go to court. After WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke directly with Seabreeze Roofing's owner, a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized was delivered within an hour, lifting the lien from McCoy's property. The contractor also sent crews back to fix the two problem areas on his roof, completing the work about an hour after McCoy received the waiver.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward on Midway Road expansion and new Florida Turnpike interchange
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie is taking steps to improve traffic flow and regional connectivity as the city continues to experience growth. The City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to transfer 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation. This land will support the construction of a new partial interchange on the Florida Turnpike, a project that remains in the design phase.

Scott Samples, the city's strategic communications manager, explained the reasoning behind the interchange project. "There's a pretty significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie," Samples said. The new interchange is designed to improve accessibility for residents and visitors as the area grows. According to Samples, the city is working "to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years." The City Council will vote on final approval to transfer the land at an upcoming meeting.

The interchange is part of a larger effort by FDOT to improve the region. The Florida Department of Transportation is overseeing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project, which aims to reduce congestion and enhance safety. Currently, crews are working on the first phase of the project, expanding the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, which will widen the road from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, is still in the design stage. Construction on that phase is expected to begin in summer 2027.

The Midway Road Widening Project includes multiple improvements beyond just adding lanes. FDOT is working to improve the Turnpike bridge and will add bike and pedestrian paths alongside sidewalks to encourage alternative transportation. While construction can be disruptive for nearby residents, many understand its necessity. One Port St. Lucie resident acknowledged the inconvenience but recognized the benefits, saying "We definitely needed it to be expanded. It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." As the project progresses through its various phases and design stages, the improvements to Midway Road and the new Turnpike interchange are expected to better serve Port St. Lucie's current needs and support continued development in the coming decades.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Marine Unit rescues two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two people were pulled from the water Wednesday after their small motorized boat took on water and sank. Both wore life jackets that kept them afloat until help arrived.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1, thanks to a quick response from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit and their decision to wear life jackets. The Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save lives.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie driver held teens at gunpoint after Orbeez pellet shooting incident
cards.teaser: A driver confronted teenagers with a gun after they shot Orbeez pellets at his vehicle in Port St. Lucie, according to police.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police responded to an incident Thursday where a driver held teenagers at gunpoint. The confrontation occurred after the teens shot Orbeez pellets at the driver's car.

Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. The case involves both the pellet shooting and the driver's response with a firearm.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce authorities seize methamphetamine and MDMA in drug trafficking bust
cards.teaser: Authorities in Fort Pierce arrested a suspect after discovering trafficking amounts of illegal drugs.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce law enforcement seized 60.5 grams of methamphetamine and 43.5 grams of MDMA in a drug trafficking bust Thursday. The quantities meet Florida's threshold for trafficking charges.

Authorities have not released additional details about the arrest or the suspect's identity. The case remains under investigation.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested on child pornography charges
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested a Fort Pierce resident on child pornography charges this week.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce man faces child pornography charges following an investigation by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. The arrest occurred Thursday.

The sheriff's office has not released the suspect's name or the specific charges filed.

cards.headline: Endangered snail kites spotted in St. Lucie County community
cards.teaser: Residents have observed endangered snail kites in a St. Lucie County neighborhood, marking a notable wildlife sighting.
cards.body:
Endangered snail kites have been spotted in a St. Lucie County community. The birds are protected under federal endangered species laws.

Snail kites are specialized raptors that feed primarily on apple snails. Their presence indicates suitable wetland habitat in the area.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police officer dedicates career to helping homeless residents
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce officer has spent years working to provide assistance and hope to people experiencing homelessness in the city.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce police officer has made helping homeless residents a focus of his law enforcement career. The officer works to connect people experiencing homelessness with resources and assistance.

The officer's approach emphasizes building trust and offering pathways to stability. His efforts reflect ongoing work by Fort Pierce police to address homelessness through community engagement rather than enforcement alone.

hero.headline: Two people rescued after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
hero.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit deputies rescued two boaters from the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday after their small motorized vessel sank.
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said in a Facebook post that the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life, adding that they are grateful the call ended safely and proud of the swift response by Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie is moving forward with infrastructure improvements to accommodate the city's rapid growth. Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange project. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city and is designed to accommodate growth over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website, the second phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial Turnpike interchange is also in the design phase. The project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County planning board recommends denial of AI data center near Arden
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School in western Palm Beach County. The recommendation followed a nearly five-hour public hearing at the Vista Center that drew more than 100 attendees, with more than 40 residents speaking during public comment. The proposed facility would be built approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and the recently opened Saddle View Elementary School. The project now heads to the Palm Beach County Commission, which will make the final decision during a July 15 public hearing.

One of the central issues during Thursday's hearing was how the project should be classified under the county's land development code. Board members questioned whether the proposed data center qualifies as light industrial or should instead be considered heavy industrial. Under county regulations, light industrial uses cannot create impacts beyond their property lines. Board members said they were not presented with enough evidence to conclude the facility would meet that standard. Project developer Ernie Cox said he was disappointed by the board's recommendation but plans to use the feedback from Thursday's hearing to strengthen his case before county commissioners. County commissioners are expected to consider both the planning staff's recommendation for approval and the Planning and Zoning Board's recommendation for denial when they make the final decision on July 15.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed, roof fixed after WPTV investigation
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, said a roofing contractor left him with unfinished repairs and a lien on his home before WPTV stepped in.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season. McCoy made six payments to the company totaling more than $17,000 and was mostly satisfied with the work, except for two holes left unfinished on the back of his home. After the company stopped responding to his calls, emails, and in-person visits beginning in January, McCoy received letters from Gulfeagle Supply warning that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien on his home. The lien stated that Gulfeagle Supply had furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing but was not paid for those supplies. McCoy said he worried about having to hire an attorney or go to court.

WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey visited Seabreeze Roofing and spoke with the owner. Within an hour, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized, removing the lien from his property. The contractor also agreed to send crews back to fix the two problem areas on his roof. About an hour after McCoy received the waiver, he sent WPTV a photo showing crews working on his roof to complete the repairs.

cards.headline: Delray Beach area golf training center delayed three months after contractor problems
cards.teaser: Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, said contractor problems delayed his opening by three months.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a virtual golf training and performance center preparing to open near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, faced a three-month delay after problems with his contractor. Although the contractor was licensed, Molen said the work ultimately had to be redone, creating a costly domino effect. He estimated the issues cost him about $90,000, not including revenue lost during the delays or the added expense of bringing in another contractor to fix the problems. "It was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall," Molen explained.

Code Pro of the Palm Beaches founder David Allan said contractor-related issues are impacting a significant number of people across Palm Beach County, with an estimated 25 to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners facing major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have the proper licenses and insurance before any work begins. Despite the setbacks, Molen said he is focused on moving forward with Tee Box's grand opening set for July 17.

cards.headline: Autonomous transit company proposes elevated network from West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The company proposes an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, and nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Under the proposal, small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. The company describes the system as a modern alternative to traditional transit such as light rail, streetcars and people movers, functioning like a "horizontal elevator" that bypasses traffic congestion entirely.

Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost a small fraction of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail discussions that carried estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Gettinger emphasized the service would be priced at transit levels rather than private rideshare rates. Funding could potentially come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal. If commissioners move forward, the county could seek competing bids and a planning and design contract could potentially be awarded later this year.
